newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia airport plans 2.2 bln rgt Islamic bonds.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia airport plans 2.2 bln rgt Islamic bonds.

text.p: Malaysia's new Kuala Lumpur International Airport Bhd (KLIA) is planning to raise 2.2 billion ringgit from two Islamic bond issues, bank treasury dealers said on Thursday.

They said the first tranche of five-year bonds to raise 1.1 billion ringgit would be issued this month. The second tranche would be issued in April and would have a seven-year tenure, the dealers said.
Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd has been appointed the facilitating agent for the issue.
It is also the joint arranger along with DCB-Sakura Merchant Bankers Bhd, KAF Discounts Bhd and PhileoAllied Capital Bhd, the bank dealers said.
Bank Islam and KLIA officials declined to comment on the issues saying no agreement for the issues had been signed yet.
The sources said an agreement between the arrangers and KLIA would be signed on January 25 at the Ministry of Finance before the Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
In January last year, KLIA issued 20-year Islamic bonds to raise 2.2 billion ringgit.
Islamic bonds in Malaysia do not bear a coupon rate.
Under Islam's Shariah principles, business should be done on the basis of sale and purchase of assets. Giving loans by charging interest is considered usury.
The religion forbids investing in traditional banks, gaming and liquor companies.
However, Islamic issues, for calculation purposes, carry an internal rate of return (IRR). The first KLIA bond is expected to be issued with an IRR of 7.6 percent, the dealers said.
"Its IRR and price in the market will depend on what the features of the bond are," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
While the bond may not qualify for liquid asset status under local banking regulations, it is expected to be exempted from banks' eligible liabilities criteria.
Malaysia requires its financial institutions to maintain a certain percentage of their deposits and other liabilities in liquid, or easily tradeable, assets, usually government paper.
Eligible liabilities are deposits, investments and other outstandings of an institution. Institutions must maintain a certain percentage of their eligible liabilities as reserves.
KLIA has also applied to the government for withholding tax exemption to foreign investors in the bond, the dealers said.
The two bond issues are guaranteed by the government, the dealers said.
They said the government had cleared the first KLIA bond issue as a 16-year facility.
"This would allow KLIA, depending on its need, to reissue the bond at the end of the five-year period," one dealer said.
The new airport is being built at a cost of nine billion ringgit. It is located 70 km southwest of capital Kuala Lumpur.
In January last year, KLIA had said it has already raised 3.3 billion ringgit and needed to raise four billion more to fund the project.-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 8911)
